scope: 3.3.1. Model Performance Based on Raw Data
3.3.2. Enhanced Model Performance with Robust Scaling and Moving Average

matched: Traditional statistical models (Linear, Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet) exhibited poor predictive performance with R2 below 0.35 for Case I
XGBoost (R2 = 0.6769) and CatBoost (R2 = 0.7088) outperformed statistical models, with CatBoost achieving lowest RMSE = 3.9785
In Case II, inclusion of COD RM slightly improved model performance with CatBoost (R2 = 0.7059) and XGBoost (R2 = 0.6922) remaining top models
RMSE improvement from COD RM in Case II was marginal (from 3.9785 to 3.9980)
In Case III, Linear Regression (R2 = 0.6117) performed better than regularized models, showing stronger linear relationships for Spec. Flux
CatBoost (R2 = 0.7317) and XGBoost (R2 = 0.5797) achieved superior performance in Case III, with CatBoost reaching lowest RMSE (0.0069)
In Case IV, COD RM improved performance across all models, CatBoost achieved R2 = 0.7710 and RMSE = 0.0064
Framework achieved R2 > 0.77 with fewer input parameters than sensor-intensive approaches
Robust scaling in Case IV improved model stability and performance (CatBoost R2 = 0.7969, RMSE = 0.0060)
5-day moving average incorporated cumulative temporal dependencies, yielding R2 = 0.8374 and RMSE = 0.0054 for CatBoost (>10% improvement over raw data)
XGBoost improved to R2 = 0.7404 with moving average
Linear and Ridge models improved to R2 around 0.66
Repeated sampling tests (t-tests, confidence intervals) are not applicable on single full-scale operational time-series
CatBoost consistently outperformed all other models across all operational cases
